title: Attention kernel latency-hedging and stochastic selector for smooth fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a probabilistic/stochastic kernel selector with latency-hedging for attention kernels (FlashAttention v2/v3 and hybrid fallbacks) to reduce tail latency spikes during warmup, shape changes, and bursty multitenant load. Background: current deterministic selector sometimes causes oscillation when kernels trade-off throughput vs latency; aggressive fallbacks create transient regressions for other tenants and produce poor 99th-percentile token latency. This ticket implements a selector that samples candidate kernels based on a score distribution derived from (a) recent token latency quantiles, (b) occupancy and batch sizes, (c) KV cache hit rate, and (d) warmed-up kernel counts. Hedge requests that are predicted to be at risk of high tail latency by launching a short, timeboxed parallel probe to an alternative low-latency kernel (hedge) for the first N tokens. Key goals: reduce p99 token latency by >= 20% for affected workloads, avoid >2% throughput regression, and keep cost delta <5% on average.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout to 5% of runtime fleet completes without regressions
p99 token latency for benchmark suite A reduced by >=20% on hedged traffic
p50 latency change within +/-5% across benchmark suite B
No increase in GPU OOM events or workspace failures attributed to selector decisioning
Automatic rollback triggers if p99 increases >5% for 10 consecutive 5-minute windows
design_decisions: Use a lightweight exponential-decay window (60s) of per-kernel latency quantiles to compute scores
Compute a softmax over negative latency/penalty to derive sampling probabilities (temperature tunable via config)
Hedging implemented as parallel short-lived decode on an alternative kernel for up to first 8 tokens or 50ms, whichever comes first
Hedged response chosen only if it completes earlier for the same token index; otherwise primary kernel continues and alternative is cancelled
Introduce hysteresis bucket (three-tier) to avoid flip-flopping decisions during transient noise: warm, neutral, cold
Telemetry hooks for per-tenant and per-model kernel-choice, latency deltas, and hedged-success-rate
implementation_notes: Runtime change touches kernel selection path and decode dispatch; keep changes behind feature flag 'stochastic_selector_v1'
Add fast path in JIT scheduler to avoid allocation on high-throughput flows when selector deems single-kernel reliable
Ensure hedging respects KV cache consistency: only hedge when KV prefix length is <= configured threshold to avoid cache-miss amplification
Expose selector temperature, hedging window, and sample rate as per-tenant config in Dedicated/Private plans
Add unit tests for sampling distribution determinism under fixed RNG seed and integration tests for canary harness
test_plan: Local: deterministic unit tests for softmax sampling and hysteresis transitions
Integration: synthetic workload runner with spike and gradual ramp profiles (replay of production heatmaps), compare baseline vs selector on p50/p95/p99
Canary: 5% traffic for 48 hours, expanded to 25% contingent on no regressions
Chaos: simulate kernel slowdowns and workspace pressure to validate automatic fallback and hedging cancellation
Regression deck: run standard evals used by Runtime QA (long-context decode, short-burst chat, embeddings hotpath)
